title: subject_srv.exe — live network process at memory acquisition (PID 6160)
observation: windows.netscan shows PID 6160 (Owner="subject_srv.ex", 14-char kernel truncation of subject_srv.exe) with an ESTABLISHED TCPv4 connection: local 172.16.4.5:3262 <-> foreign 172.16.5.50:44262. The same PID also has TCPv4 and TCPv6 sockets in LISTENING state on port 3262 (0.0.0.0:3262 / :::3262).
interpretation: An ESTABLISHED connection in a netscan output is a CONFIRMED indicator that the owning process was running at the moment of memory acquisition (per Volatility3 netscan analyst note). subject_srv.exe is listed in the prd.json/IOC-correlation workload as the subject process for this investigation; its presence as a live, listening, network-connected process on a non-standard high port (3262) on a file-server host is anomalous.

title: subject_srv.exe — historical connection to 172.16.5.25:5682
observation: windows.netscan lists a CLOSED TCPv4 entry for PID 6160 (Owner="subject_srv.ex"): local 172.16.4.5:59300 <-> foreign 172.16.5.25:5682, state CLOSED, no Created timestamp available.
interpretation: CLOSED state means this connection existed prior to memory acquisition but was no longer active at capture time. It represents a prior outbound connection from subject_srv.exe to 172.16.5.25 on a non-standard port (5682), consistent with a beaconing or C2 callback pattern observed for subject_srv.exe in related host investigations. No correlate_evidence() CONFIRMED_RUNNING/HISTORICAL verdict is available for this host (verdict=ERROR due to missing pyscca and empty pslist), so this is recorded as INFERRED.

title: Suspicious port-8080 connections to 172.16.4.10 (ngentask.exe, powershell.exe)
observation: windows.netscan flags multiple historical TCPv4 connections to 172.16.4.10:8080: ngentask.exe (PID 7092, two CLOSED entries, local ports 56324/56322), powershell.exe (PID 4072, CLOSED, local port 54794), and powershell.exe (PID 3164, CLOSE_WAIT, local port 56932). The tool's own suspicion logic flags port 8080 connections as "possible C2".

This is a single-source (netscan) observation without corroborating Amcache/Prefetch/EventLog data (host is MEMORY_ONLY), so it is recorded as INFERRED/HYPOTHESIS pending further corroboration.

This is recorded as a HYPOTHESIS/evidence-gap rather than a negative finding: absence of these IOCs in the netscan table does not prove they are absent from the host overall — process-listing plugins (pslist/pstree/cmdline/dlllist/handles/malfind) all returned 0 records on this image, and disk artifacts (Amcache/Prefetch/MFT/EventLog) are not present in this case directory to corroborate. Per LAW5, this gap is documented and the investigation proceeds on the evidence that is available (netscan).
